Keep at 70°F for 3-5 days. Remove from mold and wrap in cloth for 5 more days.
At 5 weeks, pierce with 1/8 inch needle (1 hole per inch) through top and bottom.
Age at 55°F with 95% humidity. Ready at 12 weeks minimum.

recipes.title: Colby Cheese
recipes.description: A semi-hard American cheese with mild, sweet flavor and open texture. Uses washed curd technique.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Add starter culture, ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 3/8 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain most of the whey. Add cool water (60°F) to lower temperature to 80°F (washed curd). Stir 15 minutes.
Drain water. Add salt and mix well.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 4-6 weeks.

recipes.title: Pepper Jack Cheese
recipes.description: A spicy variation of Monterey Jack with added peppercorns or jalapeños.

instructions.text: Toast peppercorns in dry pan until they pop. Crack lightly with mortar and pestle.
Heat milk to 88°F (31°C). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Add starter culture, ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Add peppers and salt, mix thoroughly.
Pack into mold. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, then 40 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 1-4 months.

recipes.title: Havarti Cheese
recipes.description: A Danish semi-soft cheese with a creamy, buttery flavor and small irregular holes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C) in a water bath.
Add C101 culture. Ripen for 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently for 1 minute. Let set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Add hot water (130°F) equal to 15-25% of milk volume over 10 minutes. Target 95-100°F.
Add salt and stir curds for 15-30 minutes.
Drain curds. Pack into cloth-lined mold.
Press at 8 lbs for 15-20 min, then 16 lbs for 2 hours. Turn every 30 minutes.
Brine for 2 hours per pound.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-3 months.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese
recipes.description: A fresh, mild cheese with small curds. Can be made with small or large curds.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add starter culture. Stir well.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently.
Cover and let set at 72°F for 5-8 hours until curd forms.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes (small curd) or 1 inch cubes (large curd).
Very slowly heat to 110°F (43°C) over 30-40 minutes. Stir gently.
Hold at 110°F for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain through cheesecloth. Rinse curds with cold water.
Add salt. For creamed cottage cheese, stir in heavy cream.
Refrigerate. Use within 1-2 weeks.

recipes.title: Cream Cheese
recipes.description: A rich, spreadable fresh cheese perfect for bagels or baking.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb from 1/2 gallon milk + 1 pint cream

instructions.text: Mix milk and cream. Heat to 86°F (30°C).
Add calcium chloride, then starter culture. Stir well.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently.
Cover and let set at room temperature (68-72°F) for 12-24 hours.
When curd is thick and pulls away from sides, it's ready.
Line colander with butter muslin. Pour in curds.
Drain 12-24 hours in refrigerator until desired thickness.
Add salt and mix well. Store refrigerated up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Quark
recipes.description: A German fresh cheese, milder than yogurt. High protein, low fat. Great for baking or eating plain.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add culture. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, stir in.
Add rennet drops if using. Stir gently.
Cover and let set 12-24 hours. Temperature can drop to 68-71°F.
Curd is ready when it has a yogurt-like consistency.
Pour into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Drain 4-8 hours until desired consistency.
For smoother texture, blend or whip. Add cream for richer quark.
Refrigerate. Use within 7-10 days.

recipes.title: Crème Fraîche
recipes.description: A thick, tangy cultured cream. French classic for sauces, soups, and desserts.

instructions.text: Heat cream to 86°F (30°C).
Add buttermilk or culture. Stir well.
Cover loosely and let sit at room temperature (72°F) for 8-12 hours.
If room is cool, wrap pot in towel to maintain temperature.
Crème fraîche is ready when thickened and slightly tangy.
Stir gently and transfer to jar.
Refrigerate. Will continue to thicken. Use within 2 weeks.

notes: Use as topping for fresh fruit, in sauces, or to enrich soups

recipes.title: Baby Swiss Cheese
recipes.description: A mild, nutty cheese with small eyes (holes). Easier version of traditional Swiss Emmentaler.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C).
Add cultures (thermophilic and propionic). Ripen 15 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 120°F (49°C) over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 120°F for 30 minutes. Curds should be firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, then 25 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine for 12 hours (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Age at 55°F for 2 weeks, then at 68°F for 2-3 weeks for eye development.
Return to 55°F for 1-2 more months. Eyes should form during warm phase.

recipes.title: Gruyère Cheese
recipes.description: A classic Alpine cheese with rich, complex flavor. Minimal or no holes. Excellent for fondue.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C).
Add all cultures. Ripen 15 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd to rice-grain size (very small).
Slowly raise temperature to 122°F (50°C) over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 122°F for 45 minutes. Curds should be very firm.
Drain whey. Pack into large mold. Press at 25 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs over 24 hours.
Brine for 24 hours.
Age at 55°F, washing rind with brine weekly for first month.
Continue aging 8-14 months minimum for full flavor development.

recipes.title: Provolone Cheese
recipes.description: An Italian pasta filata (stretched curd) cheese. Can be mild or aged for sharper flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add lipase if using.
Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes.
Slowly raise to 118°F (48°C) over 30 minutes, stirring.
Let curds mat together at bottom of pot. Drain whey.
Let curd mass ripen 2-4 hours until it stretches smoothly in hot water (170°F).
Cut curd into strips. Stretch and knead in hot water until smooth.
Shape into desired form (pear, sausage, etc.). Cool in ice water.
Brine for 6-12 hours. Hang to dry. Age at 55°F for 2-12 months.

recipes.title: Asiago Cheese
recipes.description: An Italian cheese that can be fresh (Asiago Pressato) or aged (Asiago d'Allevo). Nutty, slightly sweet.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95-97°F (35-36°C).
Add cultures. This is a small amount for slow acid development. Ripen 20 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 40-50 minutes.
Cut curd to rice-grain size.
Slowly raise to 118°F (48°C) over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 118°F for 30 minutes.
Drain whey. Pack into mold. Press at 15 lbs, increasing to 40 lbs over 12 hours.
Brine for 12 hours.
Age at 55°F. Fresh Asiago: 1-2 months. Aged Asiago: 6-12 months.

recipes.title: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
recipes.description: The classic Greek village salad with chunks of feta, ripe tomatoes, cucumbers, and Kalamata olives. Authentic versions don't use lettuce.

instructions.text: Arrange tomato wedges, cucumber chunks, onion slices, and pepper rings on a large platter.
Scatter olives over the vegetables.
Place the feta slab on top (traditional) or crumble over salad.
Drizzle generously with olive oil.
Sprinkle with oregano, salt, and pepper. Add vinegar if desired.
Serve immediately with crusty bread to soak up the juices.

notes: Authentic Greek feta is made from sheep milk or a sheep/goat blend
Do not refrigerate tomatoes - use room temperature for best flavor

recipes.title: Spanakopita (Greek Spinach Pie)
recipes.description: Flaky phyllo pastry filled with spinach and feta cheese. A beloved Greek savory pie.

ingredients.prep_note: washed and chopped (or 20 oz frozen, thawed and squeezed dry)

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Sauté onion in olive oil until soft. Add spinach and cook until wilted. Let cool.
In a large bowl, combine spinach mixture, feta, ricotta (if using), eggs, scallions, dill, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Brush a 9x13 inch baking pan with butter. Layer 8 sheets of phyllo, brushing each with butter.
Spread spinach filling evenly over phyllo.
Layer remaining phyllo sheets on top, brushing each with butter.
Score the top layers into squares or diamonds with a sharp knife.
Bake 40-45 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Let cool 10 minutes before cutting along scored lines.

notes: Keep phyllo covered with damp towel while working to prevent drying
Can be assembled ahead and refrigerated before baking

recipes.title: Watermelon Feta Salad with Mint
recipes.description: A refreshing summer salad combining sweet watermelon with salty feta and fresh mint.

instructions.text: Arrange watermelon cubes on a serving platter.
Scatter feta cheese over the watermelon.
Sprinkle with torn mint leaves and red onion if using.
Drizzle with olive oil and lime juice.
Finish with a pinch of flaky salt and fresh cracked pepper.
Serve immediately while cold.

notes: Can add arugula for a peppery base
Balsamic glaze also works well as a drizzle

recipes.title: Shakshuka with Feta
recipes.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce, topped with crumbled feta. Perfect for brunch.

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper, cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and cayenne. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Make 6 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook 8-10 minutes until egg whites are set but yolks are still runny.
Crumble feta over the top and sprinkle with fresh herbs.
Serve immediately from the skillet with crusty bread.

notes: Can add harissa for extra heat
Also delicious with goat cheese instead of feta

recipes.title: Cacio e Pepe
recipes.description: A simple Roman pasta with just three ingredients: pasta, Pecorino Romano, and black pepper. Deceptively simple, requires technique.

instructions.text: Toast peppercorns in a dry skillet until fragrant. Crack coarsely with mortar and pestle.
Cook pasta in salted water until 2 minutes shy of al dente. Reserve 2 cups pasta water.
Add cracked pepper to a large skillet with 1 cup pasta water. Bring to simmer.
Transfer pasta to skillet. Toss vigorously, adding pasta water as needed.
Remove from heat. Add Pecorino gradually, tossing constantly to create a creamy emulsion.
The cheese should melt into a sauce, not clump. Add more pasta water if too thick.
Serve immediately with extra Pecorino and pepper.

notes: Do not add cheese over direct heat or it will clump
True Pecorino Romano from sheep milk is essential
Pasta water starch is key to emulsification

recipes.title: Pasta alla Gricia
recipes.source_note: Traditional Roman pasta - the 'mother' of carbonara and amatriciana
recipes.description: Roman pasta with guanciale and Pecorino Romano. Considered the ancestor of both carbonara and amatriciana.

instructions.text: Cook guanciale in a cold skillet over medium heat until fat renders and meat is crispy, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook pasta in salted water until 2 minutes shy of al dente. Reserve 2 cups pasta water.
Add 1/2 cup pasta water to the skillet with guanciale. Add cracked pepper.
Transfer pasta to skillet. Toss vigorously over medium heat.
Remove from heat. Gradually add Pecorino, tossing constantly.
Add pasta water as needed to create a creamy coating.
Serve immediately with extra cheese and pepper.

notes: Guanciale is cured pork jowl - essential for authentic flavor
No onions, no tomatoes - that would make it amatriciana

recipes.title: Pecorino with Honey and Walnuts
recipes.description: A simple Italian appetizer pairing sharp Pecorino with sweet honey and crunchy walnuts.

instructions.text: Arrange Pecorino wedges on a serving board.
Scatter toasted walnuts around the cheese.
Drizzle honey generously over the cheese.
Add pear slices if using.
Serve with crusty bread or crackers.

notes: Use aged Pecorino Toscano for a milder flavor or Pecorino Romano for sharper taste
Pairs beautifully with a robust red wine

recipes.title: Manchego with Membrillo (Quince Paste)
recipes.description: The classic Spanish pairing of nutty Manchego cheese with sweet quince paste. Simple perfection.

instructions.text: Arrange Manchego slices on a serving board.
Place membrillo slices alongside the cheese.
Scatter Marcona almonds around the board.
Serve with crusty bread. Instruct guests to pair a piece of cheese with membrillo in each bite.

notes: True Manchego is made only from Manchega sheep milk in La Mancha, Spain
Look for Denominación de Origen label for authentic Manchego

recipes.title: Manchego Croquetas
recipes.description: Crispy fried croquettes filled with creamy béchamel and Manchego cheese. A beloved Spanish bar snack.

instructions.text: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in warm milk. Cook, stirring constantly, until very thick, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in Manchego, nutmeg, salt, and pepper until cheese melts.
Spread mixture in a baking dish. Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Shape cold mixture into small cylinders or ovals using wet hands.
Dip each croqueta in beaten egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. Double-coat for extra crunch.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry croquetas in batches until golden, about 2-3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels. Serve hot.

notes: Can add jamón serrano to the béchamel
Croquetas can be frozen before frying

recipes.title: Manchego Salad with Sherry Vinaigrette
recipes.description: Mixed greens with shaved Manchego, Marcona almonds, and a sherry vinaigrette.

instructions.text: Whisk together sherry vinegar, mustard, honey, salt, and pepper.
Slowly whisk in olive oil to emulsify.
Place greens in a large bowl. Toss with enough vinaigrette to lightly coat.
Divide among plates. Top with Manchego shavings, almonds, and dried fruit.
Drizzle with a little extra vinaigrette and serve.

notes: Sherry vinegar is key - its nutty flavor complements Manchego perfectly

recipes.title: Roquefort and Walnut Salad
recipes.description: A classic French salad with peppery greens, creamy Roquefort, and toasted walnuts.

instructions.text: Whisk together vinegar, mustard, shallot, salt, and pepper.
Gradually whisk in walnut oil.
Place greens in a large bowl. Toss with vinaigrette.
Divide among plates. Top with Roquefort, walnuts, and pear slices.
Serve immediately.

notes: Roquefort is made exclusively from raw sheep milk in caves near Roquefort-sur-Soulzon, France
Walnut oil enhances the pairing but olive oil works too

recipes.title: Steak with Roquefort Sauce
recipes.description: Pan-seared steak topped with a rich, creamy Roquefort sauce. Decadent and delicious.

instructions.text: Season steaks generously with salt and pepper. Let come to room temperature.
Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat. Sear steaks 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Transfer steaks to a plate to rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and shallot, cook 2 minutes.
Add wine and scrape up browned bits. Simmer until nearly evaporated.
Add cream and simmer until slightly thickened, about 3 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in Roquefort until melted and creamy.
Spoon sauce over steaks. Garnish with chives.

notes: Don't boil the sauce after adding cheese or it may separate
Gorgonzola or Stilton can substitute if Roquefort unavailable

recipes.title: Endive Boats with Roquefort and Pear
recipes.description: Crisp endive leaves filled with Roquefort, pear, and walnuts. An elegant appetizer.

instructions.text: Blend Roquefort and cream cheese until smooth.
Fold in half the diced pear and half the walnuts.
Spoon or pipe mixture into endive leaves.
Top each with remaining pear, walnuts, and a drizzle of honey.
Garnish with snipped chives.
Arrange on platter and serve immediately.

notes: Can substitute radicchio cups if endive unavailable
Prepare filling ahead, assemble just before serving

recipes.title: Grilled Halloumi Salad
recipes.description: Warm grilled halloumi over fresh vegetables with a lemon herb dressing. The cheese gets beautifully golden and squeaky.

instructions.text: Whisk together 2 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, mint, oregano, salt, and pepper for dressing.
Combine greens, tomatoes, cucumber, onion, and olives in a large bowl.
Brush halloumi slices with remaining olive oil.
Grill or pan-fry halloumi 2-3 minutes per side until golden with grill marks.
Toss salad with dressing and divide among plates.
Top with warm halloumi and serve immediately.

notes: Halloumi must be served warm - it becomes tough when cold
Can also add watermelon for a sweet contrast

recipes.title: Halloumi and Vegetable Skewers
recipes.description: Colorful grilled skewers with halloumi and Mediterranean vegetables. Perfect for summer barbecues.

instructions.text: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes (or use metal).
Combine olive oil, garlic, oregano, lemon zest, salt, and pepper.
Thread halloumi and vegetables alternately onto skewers.
Brush skewers generously with the oil mixture.
Grill over medium-high heat 3-4 minutes per side until cheese is golden and vegetables are tender.
Serve hot with tzatziki or hummus.

notes: Don't overcook or halloumi becomes rubbery
Works great on indoor grill pan too

recipes.title: Saag Paneer (Spinach with Cheese)
recipes.description: Cubes of paneer in a creamy spinach sauce. A beloved vegetarian dish from North India.

instructions.text: Blanch spinach in boiling water 2 minutes. Drain and blend to a smooth puree.
Fry paneer cubes in 1 tbsp ghee until golden. Set aside.
Heat remaining ghee. Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle.
Add onion and cook until golden. Add garlic, ginger, and green chilies.
Add turmeric and garam masala. Cook 1 minute.
Add spinach puree and salt. Simmer 5-7 minutes.
Add cream and paneer. Simmer 5 minutes more.
Serve hot with naan or rice.

notes: Can substitute mustard greens for spinach (then called sarson ka saag)
Adjust chilies to taste

recipes.title: Paneer Tikka Masala
recipes.description: Grilled paneer cubes in a rich, creamy tomato sauce. The vegetarian version of the famous tikka masala.

instructions.text: Marinate paneer in yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, half the chili powder, and salt. Rest 20 minutes.
Grill or pan-fry marinated paneer until charred spots appear. Set aside.
Heat butter and oil. Sauté onion until golden.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Add remaining spices (chili powder, garam masala, cumin). Cook 1 minute.
Add tomato puree and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add cream and kasuri methi. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add grilled paneer and simmer 5 minutes more.
Garnish with cilantro. Serve with naan or rice.

notes: Crushing kasuri methi between palms releases more flavor
Can use canned tomatoes blended smooth

recipes.title: Matar Paneer (Peas and Cheese Curry)
recipes.description: A comforting North Indian curry with paneer and green peas in a tomato-based sauce.

instructions.text: Lightly fry paneer cubes until golden. Set aside.
Heat oil, add cumin seeds. When they splutter, add onion puree.
Cook onion until golden, about 8-10 minutes.
Add ginger-garlic paste, cook 2 minutes.
Add all spices (turmeric, coriander, chili powder). Cook 1 minute.
Add tomato puree and salt. Cook until oil separates, about 10 minutes.
Add water and peas. Simmer until peas are tender, about 5 minutes.
Add paneer and garam masala. Simmer 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro. Serve with roti or rice.

recipes.title: Ricotta Stuffed Shells
recipes.description: Jumbo pasta shells filled with seasoned ricotta and mozzarella, baked in marinara sauce.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
Cook shells according to package, slightly underdone. Drain and cool.
Mix ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, Parmesan, egg, parsley, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Spread 1 cup marinara in bottom of 9x13 baking dish.
Fill each shell with ricotta mixture and arrange in dish.
Pour remaining sauce over shells. Top with remaining mozzarella.
Cover with foil. Bake 30 minutes.
Remove foil and bake 15 minutes more until bubbly and golden.

notes: Can add cooked spinach or Italian sausage to filling
Freezes well before baking

recipes.title: Lemon Ricotta Pasta
recipes.description: A light, creamy pasta with lemon and ricotta. Ready in 20 minutes.

instructions.text: Cook pasta in salted water. Reserve 1 cup pasta water before draining.
Sauté garlic in olive oil for 30 seconds.
In a bowl, whisk ricotta, lemon zest, lemon juice, and 1/2 cup pasta water.
Toss hot pasta with ricotta mixture and garlic oil.
Add Parmesan and toss. Add more pasta water if needed.
Season with salt and pepper. Top with basil.
Serve immediately with extra Parmesan.

notes: Add peas or asparagus for a spring version
Fresh ricotta makes a big difference

recipes.title: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes
recipes.description: Light, fluffy pancakes made with ricotta cheese and lemon zest. A weekend treat.

instructions.text: Whisk egg yolks, ricotta, milk, lemon zest, and vanilla.
In another bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients to wet and stir until just combined.
Beat egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold into batter gently.
Heat griddle over medium-low heat. Add butter.
Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form, flip.
Cook until golden on second side.
Serve with maple syrup and fresh berries.

notes: Low heat is key - these burn easily due to sugar
Folding in egg whites makes them extra fluffy

recipes.title: Classic Tiramisu
recipes.description: The beloved Italian dessert with layers of coffee-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cream.

instructions.text: Whisk egg yolks and sugar over simmering water until thick and pale, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat. Add mascarpone and vanilla, whisk until smooth. Let cool.
Whip heavy cream to stiff peaks. Fold into mascarpone mixture.
Combine cooled coffee and Marsala in a shallow dish.
Quickly dip ladyfingers in coffee (don't soak). Layer in 9x13 dish.
Spread half the mascarpone cream over ladyfingers.
Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and remaining cream.
Cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Dust with cocoa powder before serving.

notes: Use room temperature mascarpone for smoothest texture
Best made a day ahead for flavors to meld

recipes.title: Pasta with Mascarpone and Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.description: A luxuriously creamy pasta with mascarpone, sun-dried tomatoes, and fresh basil.

instructions.text: Cook pasta in salted water. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Sauté garlic in olive oil until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Add sun-dried tomatoes and cook 1 minute.
Reduce heat. Stir in mascarpone until melted.
Add drained pasta and toss. Add pasta water to thin sauce if needed.
Toss in Parmesan and basil.
Season with salt and pepper. Top with pine nuts if using.

notes: Don't boil the mascarpone or it may separate
Add cooked chicken for a heartier dish

recipes.title: French Onion Soup
recipes.description: Deeply caramelized onions in rich beef broth, topped with crusty bread and melted Gruyère.

instructions.text: Melt butter with oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add onions and sugar. Cook, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized, 45-60 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over onions and stir 2 minutes.
Add wine and scrape up browned bits. Cook until evaporated.
Add broth, thyme, and bay leaf. Simmer 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Remove thyme and bay leaf.
Preheat broiler. Ladle soup into oven-safe bowls.
Top each with bread slices and generous Gruyère.
Broil until cheese is bubbly and golden. Serve immediately.

notes: Don't rush the onion caramelization - it's the key to flavor
Swiss cheese can substitute for Gruyère

recipes.title: Classic Swiss Cheese Fondue
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss fondue with Gruyère and Emmental, white wine, and kirsch. Perfect for sharing.

instructions.text: Rub fondue pot with cut garlic. Discard garlic.
Add wine and lemon juice. Heat over medium until simmering.
Toss cheeses with cornstarch.
Add cheese by handfuls, stirring constantly in a figure-8 motion.
Wait for each addition to melt before adding more.
Once smooth, stir in kirsch, nutmeg, and pepper.
Transfer to fondue pot over low flame.
Serve with bread cubes for dipping. Stir occasionally.

notes: If fondue gets too thick, add a splash of warm wine
Also great with apple slices, vegetables, or small potatoes

recipes.title: Baked Brie with Honey and Nuts
recipes.description: Warm, gooey brie topped with honey, walnuts, and fresh rosemary. An irresistible appetizer.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Place brie on a small baking dish or oven-safe plate.
Score the top rind in a crosshatch pattern (optional - helps cheese ooze).
Bake 12-15 minutes until soft and gooey inside.
Drizzle with honey and top with nuts and rosemary.
Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Serve immediately with crackers or bread.

notes: Don't overbake or cheese will run everywhere
Can add fig jam or dried cranberries

recipes.title: Brie en Croûte
recipes.description: Brie wrapped in golden puff pastry with a layer of jam. Impressive yet easy.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Line baking sheet with parchment.
Roll puff pastry slightly larger if needed.
Spread jam on top of brie.
Place brie jam-side down in center of pastry.
Fold pastry up and over brie, pleating to enclose. Trim excess.
Flip seam-side down onto baking sheet.
Brush with egg wash. Score decorative pattern if desired.
Bake 20-25 minutes until pastry is deep golden.
Let rest 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Letting it rest prevents cheese from running out when cut
Can add prosciutto or dried fruit inside

recipes.title: Labneh Dip with Za'atar and Olive Oil
recipes.description: Creamy strained yogurt cheese drizzled with olive oil and za'atar. Essential Middle Eastern mezze.

instructions.text: Spread labneh on a plate or shallow bowl, creating a well in the center.
Pool olive oil in the well.
Sprinkle generously with za'atar.
Add mint and pine nuts if using.
Finish with Aleppo pepper.
Serve with warm pita for scooping.

notes: Za'atar is a blend of thyme, sumac, and sesame - essential for this dish
Can shape labneh into balls and roll in za'atar for a different presentation

recipes.title: Traditional Feta (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: Authentic Greek PDO feta requires at least 70% sheep's milk
recipes.description: Authentic Greek feta made primarily from sheep's milk, as protected by EU designation. Tangy, crumbly, and brined.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2 lbs from 2 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk (and goat's milk if using) to 86°F (30°C).
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk. Stir well.
Dissolve lipase in 1/4 cup cool water. Add to milk and stir.
Sprinkle starter culture over surface. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, then stir. Ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently for 30 seconds. Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir curds for 20 minutes while maintaining 86°F. Curds will firm up.
Line a colander with cheesecloth. Drain curds.
Transfer to feta molds or form into blocks. Let drain at room temperature 24 hours, turning every few hours.
Cut into blocks and salt all surfaces generously. Let drain 2-3 more days, turning and re-salting daily.
Prepare brine: dissolve 1/2 lb salt per gallon of water. Add a splash of whey.
Submerge feta in brine. Age in refrigerator for minimum 30 days (60+ days for fuller flavor).

notes: True Greek feta PDO requires minimum 70% sheep's milk, remainder goat's milk
Sheep's milk has higher fat content than cow's milk, creating richer feta
The longer it ages in brine, the tangier and firmer it becomes

recipes.title: Pecorino Romano (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Italian hard cheese, made exclusively from sheep's milk
recipes.description: A hard, salty Italian cheese made from sheep's milk. Sharp and piquant, essential for pasta dishes like cacio e pepe.
recipes.servings_yield: About 3-4 lbs from 4 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 100°F (38°C) - slightly warmer than many cheeses due to sheep milk's composition.
Add thermophilic culture. Let ripen 30 minutes.
Dissolve lamb rennet paste in warm water (or use liquid rennet). Add to milk, stir 30 seconds.
Let set 20-30 minutes until firm curd forms.
Cut curd into rice-grain sized pieces (very small for this hard cheese).
Slowly raise temperature to 118°F (48°C) over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Continue stirring at 118°F for 45 minutes until curds are very firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into large mold. Press at 25 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs over 24 hours.
Remove from mold. Rub all surfaces with salt. Place on aging board.
Salt rub daily for first week, then weekly for first month.
Age at 55°F with 85% humidity. Turn weekly.
Minimum aging: 5 months for table cheese, 8-12 months for grating cheese.

notes: Lamb rennet paste gives traditional sharp, piquant flavor
'Pecora' means sheep in Italian - this cheese can only be made from sheep's milk
The longer it ages, the harder and more intense the flavor

recipes.title: Manchego-Style Cheese (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.attribution: Based on traditional La Mancha methods
recipes.source_note: True Manchego is made only from Manchega sheep milk in La Mancha, Spain
recipes.description: A firm, buttery Spanish cheese with a distinctive herringbone rind pattern. Nutty and slightly tangy.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2-3 lbs from 3 gallons sheep's milk

ingredients.prep_note: Manchega breed preferred, or any sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add mesophilic culture. Let ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4 inch cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 104°F (40°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Continue stirring at 104°F for 30 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain whey. Pack curds into Manchego mold (with traditional zigzag pattern).
Press at 10 lbs for 1 hour, then 25 lbs for 6-12 hours.
Remove from mold. Brine for 12 hours (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Air dry 2-3 days until rind forms.
Age at 55°F with 85% humidity. Can rub with olive oil for traditional finish.
Fresco: 2 weeks. Semi-curado: 3-6 months. Curado: 6-12 months. Viejo: 12+ months.

notes: The zigzag rind pattern comes from traditional esparto grass molds
True DO Manchego comes only from Manchega sheep in La Mancha region
Sheep's milk gives Manchego its distinctive rich, lanolin-y undertone

recipes.title: Roquefort-Style Blue Cheese (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: True Roquefort is made from raw Lacaune sheep milk and aged in caves near Roquefort-sur-Soulzon, France
recipes.description: A tangy, creamy blue cheese made from sheep's milk. Rich and complex with distinctive blue-green veining.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2-3 lbs from 3 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add calcium chloride if needed.
Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 90 minutes for a moist curd.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Handle very gently to preserve moisture.
Let curds rest in whey 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Gently ladle curds into tall cylindrical mold without pressing.
Let drain at room temperature 24-48 hours, turning every few hours.
Remove from mold. Salt all surfaces. Let drain 2 more days.
Pierce cheese with sterilized needle from top and bottom (holes about 1 inch apart) to allow air entry for blue mold development.
Age at 50°F with 95% humidity. The high humidity is crucial.
Blue veining should develop within 30-60 days.
Wrap in foil when veining is established. Continue aging 3-6 months total.

notes: True Roquefort must be made from raw milk of Lacaune sheep
The caves of Roquefort have natural Penicillium roqueforti
High humidity and cool temperatures are essential for proper mold development
Sheep's milk gives Roquefort its distinctive rich, tangy character

recipes.title: Ricotta Salata (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: A pressed, salted, aged ricotta made from sheep's milk whey
recipes.description: A firm, salted ricotta that can be sliced or grated. Milky and slightly tangy - traditional Sicilian cheese.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb from whey of 3 gallons sheep's milk

ingredients.prep_note: leftover from making other sheep's milk cheese
dissolved in 2 tbsp water, or use lemon juice

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk whey to 185-195°F (85-90°C). Add the cup of fresh milk if using.
When temperature is reached, add citric acid solution and stir gently.
Small curds will form and rise to the surface. Remove from heat.
Let rest 10 minutes, then skim curds into a ricotta mold or cheesecloth-lined colander.
Drain 2-3 hours until curds hold together.
Mix salt thoroughly into the curds.
Pack into a small cheese mold. Press at 5 lbs for 12 hours.
Remove from mold. Place on a drying mat.
Age at 55°F with 75% humidity for 3-4 weeks minimum.
Turn daily for first week, then every few days.
The cheese will develop a thin rind and firm texture suitable for slicing or grating.

notes: Ricotta salata means 'salted ricotta'
The sheep's milk whey gives it a richer, more complex flavor than cow's milk ricotta
Can be grated over pasta like Pecorino, or sliced for salads

recipes.title: Kasseri Cheese (Sheep's Milk)
recipes.source_note: A semi-hard pasta filata cheese made from sheep's milk
recipes.description: A Greek stretched-curd cheese similar to provolone but made from sheep's milk. Tangy and slightly sharp.
recipes.servings_yield: About 2 lbs from 2 gallons sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 90°F (32°C). Add calcium chloride and lipase if using.
Add thermophilic culture. Let ripen 45 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes.
Slowly raise temperature to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain most of the whey. Let curds mat together.
Let curd mass acidify for 2-4 hours until it stretches smoothly in 170°F water.
Cut curd into strips. Stretch and knead in hot water (170°F) until smooth and shiny.
Form into a ball or loaf shape. Cool in cold water.
Brine for 8-12 hours (1 lb salt per gallon water).
Air dry until rind forms, about 1-2 days.
Age at 55°F for 2-4 months. Can be waxed after rind forms.

notes: Kasseri is a 'pasta filata' (stretched curd) cheese like mozzarella and provolone
The sheep's milk gives it a richer, tangier flavor than cow's milk versions
Traditional for Greek saganaki (fried cheese)

recipes.title: Simple Fresh Sheep's Milk Cheese
recipes.source_note: A simple fresh cheese showcasing the rich flavor of sheep's milk
recipes.description: A quick, fresh cheese that highlights the naturally rich, sweet flavor of sheep's milk. Ready to eat in hours.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1.5 lbs from 1 gallon sheep's milk

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 180-185°F (82-85°C), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Add lemon juice or vinegar. Stir gently.
Let sit undisturbed for 15 minutes. Curds will separate from whey.
Line a colander with butter muslin or cheesecloth.
Gently ladle curds into lined colander.
Sprinkle salt over curds. Add herbs if desired.
Gather cloth and hang to drain, or press lightly in mold for 2-3 hours.
Enjoy fresh at room temperature or chilled. Use within 1 week.

notes: Sheep's milk has nearly twice the fat of cow's milk, yielding a richer cheese
The natural sweetness of sheep's milk shines in this simple preparation
Try drizzling with honey and walnuts for a traditional Mediterranean treat

recipes.title: Oscypek-Style Smoked Sheep Cheese
recipes.source_note: Traditional Polish smoked cheese from the Tatra Mountains, made from sheep's milk
recipes.description: A smoked sheep's milk cheese with a decorative spindle shape. Slightly salty with a rich smoky flavor.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1.5 lbs from 2 gallons sheep's milk

ingredients.prep_note: can blend with up to 40% cow's milk traditionally

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add starter culture. Let ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until firm curd.
Cut curd into small pieces. Stir gently.
Slowly raise temperature to 95°F (35°C) over 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Work curds by hand, kneading and squeezing out moisture.
Add salt and knead into the curd mass.
Shape into traditional spindle form (pointed at both ends) or decorative molds.
Press by hand to create decorative patterns on surface.
Let dry at room temperature for 24 hours.
Cold smoke at 70-90°F (21-32°C) for 6-12 hours until golden brown.
Age 2-3 weeks or enjoy fresh after smoking.

notes: True Oscypek has EU Protected Designation of Origin
Traditionally made in wooden molds with carved decorative patterns
The smoking gives it a beautiful golden-brown rind
Slice and grill on a hot pan until slightly melted

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Cream Cheese (Yogurt Method)
recipes.source_note: Based on traditional labneh-style straining adapted for sheep's milk yogurt
recipes.description: A simple two-ingredient sheep's milk cream cheese made by straining sheep's milk yogurt. Yields a pillowy, tangy spread with a mildly sheepy flavor.

instructions.text: Place yogurt in a bowl and add salt. Whisk briskly for about 30 seconds until well combined.
Line a fine-mesh strainer or colander with 2-3 layers of cheesecloth or butter muslin. Set over a deep bowl to catch the whey.
Pour the salted yogurt into the lined strainer. Gather the edges of the cheesecloth and tie them together to form a bundle.
Place in the refrigerator and allow to drain for 36-48 hours. The longer it drains, the thicker and more cream cheese-like it becomes.
Check consistency after 36 hours. For spreadable cream cheese, stop when it holds its shape but is still soft.
Transfer to an airtight container. Store refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Save the whey for baking, smoothies, or soaking grains
For flavored varieties, fold in herbs, garlic, chives, or chili after draining
Sheep's milk yogurt produces a richer, tangier cream cheese than cow's milk
If sheep's milk yogurt isn't available, you can make it from sheep's milk using yogurt starter

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Cream Cheese (Traditional Method)
recipes.source_note: Traditional cream cheese making adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Rich, tangy cream cheese made from sheep's milk using the acid-set method. Sheep's milk produces an exceptionally creamy result with higher fat content than cow's milk versions.

ingredients.prep_note: preferably sheep's milk cream if available

instructions.text: Pour sheep's milk and cream into a heavy-bottomed pot (not copper or cast iron). Add salt and stir to combine.
Heat slowly over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent scorching. This should take about 30 minutes.
Monitor temperature with a thermometer. Heat to 185°F (85°C). Do not let it boil.
Remove from heat. Slowly pour in the lemon juice while stirring gently.
Let sit undisturbed for 10 minutes. The milk should separate into curds and whey.
If milk hasn't separated after 10 minutes, add the tablespoon of vinegar and stir gently. Wait another 5 minutes.
Line a colander with 4 layers of cheesecloth. Set over a large bowl.
Gently ladle the curds into the cheesecloth. Let drain for 1 hour at room temperature.
Gather cheesecloth edges, tie, and hang over the bowl or refrigerate in the strainer for 4-6 hours until desired consistency.
Transfer drained cheese to a food processor. Blend until smooth and creamy, scraping down sides as needed.
Taste and adjust salt. Transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate.

notes: Do NOT use ultra-pasteurized milk - it will not curdle properly
Sheep's milk has about twice the fat of cow's milk, yielding richer cheese
Fresh cream cheese is best used within 1-2 weeks
For a tangier flavor, add a bit more lemon juice
The whey can be saved for baking bread or adding to soups

recipes.title: Cultured Sheep's Milk Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Authentic cultured cream cheese method using sheep's milk
recipes.description: Authentic cultured cream cheese using sheep's milk and mesophilic starter for complex flavor development. This method produces the most authentic cream cheese taste.

instructions.text: Combine sheep's milk and cream in a pot. Warm gently to 75°F (24°C).
Sprinkle mesophilic starter over surface. Let rehydrate 2 minutes, then stir gently to incorporate.
Add diluted rennet and stir gently with an up-and-down motion for 30 seconds.
Cover and let culture at room temperature (70-75°F) for 12-14 hours or overnight until set like yogurt.
The curd is ready when it pulls away cleanly from the sides and whey pools on top.
Line a colander with butter muslin. Gently ladle curds into the muslin without breaking them up too much.
Tie corners of muslin and hang to drain at room temperature for 6-8 hours, or refrigerate overnight.
When cheese reaches desired consistency (thick but still spreadable), transfer to a bowl.
Add salt and mix well. For extra smooth texture, blend briefly in food processor.
Pack into containers and refrigerate. Best after chilling for several hours.

notes: The cultured method develops more complex, tangy flavors than acid-set
Use only 2 drops of rennet - too much creates a rubbery texture
Sheep's milk cream cheese will be yellower than cow's milk version
Keeps refrigerated for 2-3 weeks
Can be flavored with herbs, garlic, honey, or fruit after draining

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Ricotta
recipes.source_note: Ricotta means 're-cooked' - traditionally made from whey
recipes.description: Fresh, creamy ricotta from sheep's milk. Richer and sweeter than cow's milk ricotta with a delicate, slightly nutty flavor.

instructions.text: Pour sheep's milk and cream into a heavy pot. Add salt.
Heat slowly over medium heat to 185-190°F (85-88°C), stirring occasionally.
Remove from heat. Add lemon juice and stir gently once.
Let sit undisturbed 10-15 minutes until curds form.
Line a colander with cheesecloth. Gently ladle curds into cloth.
Drain 1-2 hours for creamy ricotta, longer for drier texture.
Transfer to container. Refrigerate up to 1 week.

notes: Sheep's milk ricotta is naturally sweeter and richer
Use within a week for best flavor
Perfect for lasagna, cannoli, or eating fresh with honey

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Cottage Cheese
recipes.description: Creamy cottage cheese made from sheep's milk with small, tender curds. Higher in protein and fat than cow's milk version.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 72°F (22°C). Add starter, stir, let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet, stir gently. Cover and let set 4-6 hours until firm.
Cut curd into 1/2 inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Slowly heat to 110°F (43°C) over 30-40 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 110°F for 20-30 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain through cheesecloth. Rinse curds with cold water.
Toss curds with salt and cream. Refrigerate.

notes: Small curd develops at lower cooking temps, large curd at higher
Add herbs or fruit for variations

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Quark
recipes.source_note: Traditional quark adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Smooth, tangy fresh cheese similar to Greek yogurt but milder. Sheep's milk adds richness and depth.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add starter, stir. Add diluted rennet, stir briefly.
Cover and let culture 12-18 hours at room temp until set like yogurt.
Ladle into cheesecloth-lined strainer.
Drain 6-12 hours until desired thickness.
Blend smooth if desired. Season with salt to taste.

notes: Use for baking, spreads, or eating plain
Can substitute for sour cream or cream cheese in recipes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Mascarpone
recipes.description: Ultra-rich, buttery mascarpone made from sheep's milk cream. Perfect for tiramisu and desserts.

instructions.text: Heat cream in double boiler to 185°F (85°C).
Add lemon juice, stir gently. Hold temp 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let cool 30 minutes.
Pour into cheesecloth-lined strainer over bowl.
Refrigerate and drain 12-24 hours.
Transfer thickened mascarpone to container.

notes: Sheep cream mascarpone is exceptionally rich
Use within 1 week
Perfect for tiramisu, cheesecake, pasta sauces

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Fromage Blanc
recipes.source_note: Traditional fromage blanc adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Silky, spreadable fresh cheese with mild tang. Sheep's milk version is creamier with subtle sweetness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C).
Add culture, stir thoroughly.
Cover and let set 12-14 hours at 72°F until thick like yogurt.
Gently ladle into butter muslin-lined colander.
Drain 6-12 hours until spreadable consistency.
Mix in salt. Add herbs or honey for variations.

notes: Wonderful with fresh fruit or on toast
Mix with herbs for savory spread
Base for many French desserts

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Mozzarella
recipes.source_note: Traditional mozzarella adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Fresh stretched-curd mozzarella from sheep's milk. Creamier and richer than cow's milk version with excellent melt.

instructions.text: Add citric acid solution to cold milk. Heat to 90°F (32°C), stirring.
Remove from heat. Add rennet, stir gently 30 seconds. Cover, let set 5-10 min.
Check for clean break. Cut curd into 1-inch cubes.
Heat curds to 105°F (40°C), stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press curds together in pot.
Heat water or whey to 170°F (77°C). Submerge curd until pliable.
Stretch and fold curd until smooth and shiny. Add salt while stretching.
Form into balls. Cool in ice water bath.

notes: Sheep milk mozzarella has higher fat for better melt
Use same day for best texture
Store in whey or salted water up to 1 week

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Burrata
recipes.source_note: Traditional burrata adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Luxurious mozzarella pouch filled with stracciatella and cream. Sheep's milk makes it exceptionally rich.

instructions.text: Prepare mozzarella curd using sheep milk mozzarella recipe.
Reserve 1/4 of stretched curd. Shred into thin strips (stracciatella).
Mix stracciatella with cream and salt.
Stretch remaining curd into thin sheets.
Form pouches, fill with stracciatella mixture.
Pinch closed, forming a sealed ball.
Store in cream or brine. Consume within 2 days.

notes: Best eaten within 24 hours of making
The cream should ooze out when cut open
Serve at room temperature with tomatoes and basil

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Provolone
recipes.source_note: Traditional provolone adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Aged stretched-curd cheese with sharp, tangy flavor. Sheep's milk adds complexity and richness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 97°F (36°C). Add lipase dissolved in water. Stir.
Add starter, let ripen 30 minutes.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 30-45 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Stir gently, heat to 118°F (48°C).
Drain whey. Let curd mat and acidify until pH 5.2 (stretches in hot water).
Stretch in 170°F water until smooth. Form into traditional shapes.
Brine 12 hours per pound.
Hang to dry. Age 2-12 months in cool cave or fridge.

notes: Provolone Dolce: mild, aged 2-3 months
Provolone Piccante: sharp, aged 6-12 months
Can be smoked for additional flavor

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Scamorza
recipes.description: Pear-shaped stretched cheese, often smoked. Firmer than mozzarella with concentrated flavor.

instructions.text: Make mozzarella curd using standard method.
Stretch until very smooth and elastic.
Form into pear shape with pinched 'neck' at top.
Tie string around neck for hanging.
Hang to dry 1-2 weeks in cool area.
Optional: cold smoke for Scamorza Affumicata.

notes: Scamorza Bianca: plain white, mild
Scamorza Affumicata: smoked, deeper flavor
Great melting cheese for pizza and pasta

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Caciocavallo
recipes.source_note: Traditional caciocavallo adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Gourd-shaped aged pasta filata cheese. Name means 'cheese on horseback' from traditional drying method.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter, ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet, let set 40 minutes.
Cut curd small (1/4 inch). Cook to 118°F.
Drain and let curd acidify 3-5 hours until stretchy.
Stretch in hot water. Form into gourd shape with small ball on top.
Tie with raffia at neck. Hang in pairs over rod.
Brine 8-12 hours. Dry and age 3-6 months.

notes: Traditional shape resembles a teardrop with a topknot
Aged versions develop sharp, tangy flavor
Young versions are mild and great for grilling

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Gouda
recipes.source_note: Traditional Gouda adapted for sheep's milk (like Ewephoria)
recipes.description: Sweet, nutty washed-curd cheese. Sheep's milk version has caramel notes and rich, buttery texture.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add calcium chloride if using.
Add starter, ripen 10 minutes. Add rennet, set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with 90°F water (washing step).
Slowly heat to 100°F over 30 minutes while stirring.
Drain whey. Press curds into mold at 10 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs.
Brine 12 hours. Air dry 2-3 days.
Wax or vacuum seal. Age 2-12 months.

notes: Washing the curd removes lactose, creating sweeter cheese
Young Gouda (2 months): mild, creamy
Aged Gouda (12+ months): crystalline, caramel notes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Edam
recipes.source_note: Traditional Edam adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Mild, slightly nutty semi-hard cheese in distinctive ball shape. Lower fat than Gouda.

instructions.text: Partially skim cream from milk. Heat to 86°F.
Add starter, ripen 30 minutes. Add rennet, set 45 minutes.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Remove 1/3 whey, replace with warm water.
Heat to 100°F. Stir 30 minutes.
Press into round mold. Press 3-6 hours.
Brine 8 hours. Dry and wax with red wax.
Age 1-4 months.

notes: Traditional red wax coating
Milder than Gouda due to lower fat
Good melting cheese

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Traditional cheddar method adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Sharp, crumbly cheddar made with sheep's milk. Richer and more complex than cow's milk cheddar.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add calcium chloride and starter. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet, let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Cut curd mass into slabs.
Stack and flip slabs every 15 minutes for 2 hours (cheddaring).
Mill curd into finger-sized pieces. Mix in salt.
Press at 50 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry 3-5 days until dry to touch. Wax or bandage.
Age 3-24 months at 55°F.

notes: Cheddaring develops the signature texture
Longer aging = sharper flavor
Sheep milk cheddar develops complex, nutty notes

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Colby
recipes.source_note: Wisconsin Colby adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Mild, moist American cheese with open texture. Sheep's milk adds subtle sweetness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add annatto if using for orange color.
Add starter, ripen 45 minutes. Add rennet, set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 3/8-inch cubes.
Heat to 102°F over 30 minutes.
Drain whey to curd level. Add cold water to 80°F.
Stir 15 minutes. Drain. Add salt.
Press lightly at 20 lbs for 20 minutes, then 40 lbs for 3 hours.
Air dry, wax, age 1-3 months.

notes: Washing creates characteristic open texture
Milder than cheddar
Best at 1-2 months - doesn't improve with long aging

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Brie
recipes.source_note: Traditional Brie adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Creamy, bloomy-rind cheese with buttery interior. Sheep's milk creates an exceptionally rich, complex Brie.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add calcium chloride, starter, and P. candidum. Stir.
Ripen 90 minutes. Add rennet, let set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Brie molds. Do not press.
Flip every few hours for 24 hours as whey drains.
Salt all surfaces. Air dry 2-3 days at 50-55°F.
Age at 50-55°F, 95% humidity for 4-6 weeks until white bloom covers surface.
Wrap and refrigerate. Best at room temperature.

notes: High humidity is crucial for proper bloom development
Sheep's milk Brie will be yellower than cow's milk version
Ripe when soft throughout with slight ammonia aroma

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Camembert
recipes.source_note: Traditional Camembert adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Smaller, more intense cousin of Brie with earthy, mushroomy notes. Sheep's milk adds depth.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, P. candidum, and Geotrichum. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Let set 90 minutes.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir 20 minutes. Ladle into Camembert molds.
Flip every 2 hours for 12 hours, then twice daily.
Unmold after 2 days. Salt surfaces.
Age at 50-55°F, high humidity, for 3-5 weeks.
Wrap when fully bloomed. Enjoy at room temp.

notes: Smaller size means faster ripening than Brie
Should be gooey when fully ripe
Traditional Camembert de Normandie uses raw milk

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Coulommiers
recipes.description: The predecessor to Brie, smaller and thicker with more intense flavor. Sheep's milk version is exceptional.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and mold. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet, set 90 minutes until clean break.
Cut curd into 3/4-inch cubes.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Ladle into tall Coulommiers molds.
Flip regularly for 24 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Dry 2 days.
Age 3-4 weeks at 52°F with high humidity.

notes: Thicker than Brie, so center ripens more slowly
Original Brie-style cheese from Île-de-France region

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Gorgonzola-Style
recipes.source_note: Gorgonzola method adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Creamy Italian blue with sheep's milk richness. Develops sweet, spicy, earthy notes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and P. roqueforti. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Let set 1 hour until firm.
Cut into 1-inch cubes. Rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir 30 minutes without heating.
Drain whey. Ladle curds into tall mold without pressing.
Flip several times daily for 3-4 days.
Salt all surfaces. Pierce with needle to create air channels.
Age 3-6 months at 46-50°F, 95% humidity. Pierce again at 1 month.

notes: Dolce version: younger, creamier, milder
Piccante version: aged longer, more intense
Piercing allows oxygen in for blue mold growth

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Stilton-Style
recipes.source_note: Stilton method adapted for sheep's milk (like Lanark Blue)
recipes.description: King of English blues made with sheep's milk. Rich, creamy with bold blue veining.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and blue mold. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Set 90 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let settle 10 min.
Drain whey. Let curds mat and acidify 1-2 hours.
Mill curds. Mix with salt.
Pack loosely into tall cylindrical mold. Do not press.
Flip twice daily for 5 days. Smooth sides with knife.
Pierce all over at 6 weeks. Age 3-4 months at 50°F.

notes: True Stilton is PDO protected - this is 'Stilton-style'
Lanark Blue is a Scottish sheep's milk blue similar to this
Rubbing rind helps develop the characteristic crust

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Danish Blue Style
recipes.source_note: Danish Blue adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Sharp, salty blue cheese. Sheep's milk adds creaminess to the bold flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add lipase, starter, blue mold. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut into 1/2-inch cubes. Stir gently 15 minutes.
Drain whey. Pack curds loosely in mold.
Flip twice daily for 3 days.
Salt heavily. Pierce all surfaces.
Age 2-3 months at 50°F, high humidity.

notes: More crumbly texture than Roquefort
Very salty - use less if preferred
Great crumbled on salads

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Havarti
recipes.source_note: Traditional Havarti adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Buttery, flexible cheese with small irregular holes. Sheep's milk makes it extra creamy.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Let rest 10 min. Remove 1/3 whey, replace with warm water.
Heat slowly to 100°F over 30 minutes.
Drain. Press lightly at 8 lbs for 30 min, flip, 15 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine 12 hours. Dry and wax.
Age 2-3 months at 50°F.

notes: Can add dill, caraway, or jalapeño for flavored versions
Light pressing creates characteristic small holes
Excellent melting cheese

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Fontina
recipes.source_note: Fontina Val d'Aosta adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Nutty, earthy semi-soft cheese from the Alps. Sheep's milk adds depth and richness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 35-40 minutes.
Cut into 1/4-inch cubes.
Heat to 118°F over 45 minutes, stirring.
Let curds settle. Drain whey.
Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, 25 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine 12 hours. Dry.
Age 3-4 months, washing rind with brine weekly.

notes: True Fontina is a washed-rind cheese
Excellent fondue cheese
Develops earthy, mushroomy notes with age

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Gruyère-Style
recipes.source_note: Gruyère method adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Complex, nutty Alpine cheese. Sheep's milk creates intense, sweet-savory flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 15 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces.
Heat to 120°F over 40 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 120°F for 30 minutes, stirring.
Drain and press at 25 lbs, increasing to 50 lbs over 12 hours.
Brine 24 hours.
Age 6-12 months at 55°F, washing with brine weekly.

notes: True Gruyère is AOC protected
High cooking temp creates signature dense texture
Excellent for fondue and gratins

recipes.title: Idiazabal (Basque Smoked Sheep Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Basque sheep cheese, often smoked
recipes.description: Firm, buttery Basque cheese traditionally made from Latxa sheep milk. Often lightly smoked with cherry or beech wood.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes until firm.
Cut curd into small pieces (lentil-sized).
Heat to 104°F while stirring gently.
Drain and press firmly at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine 24 hours.
Air dry 1 week. Optional: cold smoke 12-24 hours.
Age 2-5 months at 50°F.

notes: Smoked version (ahumado) uses cherry or beech wood
Unsmoked version shows purer sheep milk flavor
PDO requires milk from Latxa or Carranzana sheep

recipes.title: Roncal (Navarre Sheep Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional cheese from Roncal Valley, Navarre
recipes.description: Hard, granular sheep cheese with intense, piquant flavor. Spain's first protected designation cheese (1981).

instructions.text: Heat raw milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 20 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd very small (rice grain size).
Heat to 104°F, stirring constantly.
Press curds by hand in mold, then press at 40 lbs for 24 hours.
Rub surface with salt over several days.
Age minimum 4 months, up to 8 for fuller flavor.

notes: PDO requires raw sheep milk from Rasa and Lacha breeds
Develops sharp, slightly spicy flavor with age
Rind should be rubbed with olive oil during aging

recipes.title: Torta del Casar (Extremadura Soft Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Unique soft cheese coagulated with thistle
recipes.description: Creamy, oozing cheese with bitter, herbaceous notes from cardoon thistle rennet. Cut top off and scoop like fondue.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 82-86°F.
Add cardoon thistle extract. Let set 60-90 minutes (longer than animal rennet).
Cut curd gently into large pieces.
Ladle into small round molds. Do not press heavily.
Salt surfaces. Flip daily for several days.
Age at 46-50°F, high humidity, minimum 60 days.
Cheese should develop soft, oozing interior with firm rind.

notes: Cardoon thistle creates unique bitter, vegetal flavor
Serve by cutting top off and scooping interior
Cannot be imported to USA (raw milk, young aging)

recipes.title: Zamorano (Castile Sheep Cheese)
recipes.description: Hard, intensely flavored cheese similar to Manchego but sharper. Made from Churra and Castellana sheep.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut into very small curds. Stir and heat to 104°F.
Press firmly at 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine 48 hours.
Age 6-12 months, coating with olive oil.

notes: Sharper and more intense than Manchego
Traditional zigzag pattern pressed into rind
PDO since 1993

recipes.title: Serra da Estrela (Portuguese Mountain Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Portuguese sheep cheese with thistle rennet
recipes.description: Portugal's most prized cheese - creamy, unctuous interior with tangy, herbaceous flavor from cardoon thistle.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 82-86°F.
Add cardoon thistle. Let set 60 minutes until soft curd forms.
Gently break curd. Do not cut into small pieces.
Ladle into cloth-lined molds. Press very gently.
Salt and flip daily for 3-4 days.
Age 30-45 days minimum at 45-50°F, high humidity.
Young cheese (Amanteigado) should be spoonable. Aged version (Velho) is firmer.

notes: PDO protected - 'King of Portuguese Cheeses'
Young version has liquid center, scooped like fondue
Thistle gives distinctive bitter, herbal notes

recipes.title: Azeitão (Portuguese Soft Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Small, creamy cheese from near Lisbon
recipes.description: Small, rich cheese with runny interior. Similar to Serra but smaller with more intense flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 82°F.
Add thistle extract. Set 45-60 minutes.
Gently cut and ladle into small molds (about 4 oz each).
Salt surfaces. Flip twice daily.
Age 20-30 days at 50°F, high humidity.

notes: Smaller and richer than Serra da Estrela
Typically 100-250g wheels
Serve at room temperature, cut top and scoop

recipes.title: Ossau-Iraty (French Basque Cheese)
recipes.description: Smooth, firm cheese with sweet, nutty, grassy notes. Made from Basco-Béarnaise and Manech sheep.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces.
Heat slowly to 104°F, stirring.
Drain and press at 25 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine 24-48 hours depending on size.
Age 3-6 months, brushing rind periodically.

notes: Pairs traditionally with cherry jam
AOC/PDO protected since 1980
Flavor is milder and sweeter than Spanish Basque cheeses

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Emmental/Swiss
recipes.source_note: Classic Swiss cheese adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Large-holed Swiss cheese made with sheep's milk. Nutty and sweet with characteristic eyes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter and P. shermanii. Ripen 15 min.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces.
Heat to 125°F over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 125°F for 30 minutes.
Press at 30 lbs increasing to 60 lbs over 24 hours.
Brine 24 hours.
Age at 55°F for 2 weeks, then 68-72°F for 3-4 weeks for eye development.
Move to 45°F for remaining 3-4 months.

notes: Warm aging period creates the characteristic holes
P. shermanii bacteria produce CO2 that forms eyes
Sheep milk creates richer, more complex Swiss

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Parmesan-Style (Pecorino Aged)
recipes.source_note: Long-aged grating cheese, sheep milk version
recipes.description: Hard, crystalline grating cheese aged 12-24 months. Intensely flavored with complex umami notes.

instructions.text: Skim cream from evening milk. Combine with morning milk.
Heat to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 15 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 15-20 minutes until firm.
Cut into tiny pieces (smaller than rice grains).
Heat to 131°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Let curds settle and mat on bottom.
Press firmly at 50-60 lbs for 24 hours, flipping several times.
Brine 3 weeks, turning daily.
Age 12-24 months at 55°F, turning and brushing weekly.

notes: Similar to aged Pecorino Romano
Develops tyrosine crystals at 18+ months
Excellent grating cheese for pasta

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk American-Style Cheese
recipes.source_note: Homemade American cheese using sheep's milk base
recipes.description: Creamy, meltable American-style cheese made from sheep's milk cheddar. Perfect for burgers and grilled cheese.

instructions.text: Combine milk, butter, and sodium citrate in a pot. Heat to 180°F.
Remove from heat. Add shredded cheese gradually, stirring constantly.
Blend with immersion blender until completely smooth.
Pour into silicone mold or lined loaf pan.
Refrigerate until firm, about 2 hours.
Slice for sandwiches. Melts beautifully.

notes: Sodium citrate is key for smooth, meltable texture
Can add turmeric for orange color
Sheep milk base makes it richer than cow's milk version

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Monterey Jack
recipes.source_note: American original adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Mild, creamy, excellent melting cheese. Sheep's milk adds subtle richness to this versatile cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F. Add starter, ripen 45 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Heat slowly to 102°F over 40 minutes.
Drain whey. Stir curds to dry slightly.
Add salt, mix. Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour, then 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Air dry, wax or vacuum seal. Age 1-3 months.

notes: Add jalapeños for Pepper Jack variant
Mild enough for young eating
Excellent Tex-Mex melting cheese

recipes.title: Pecorino Sardo (Sardinian Sheep Cheese)
recipes.description: Sardinia's signature cheese - firm, nutty, slightly sweet with grassy undertones.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter, ripen 20 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into small pieces (pea-sized).
Cook at 104°F for 15 minutes, stirring.
Drain and press at 25 lbs for 12 hours.
Brine 12-24 hours.
Age: Dolce 1-2 months, Maturo 4-8 months.

notes: Dolce: young, mild, table cheese
Maturo: aged, sharper, grating cheese
PDO protected

recipes.title: Graviera (Greek Gruyère-Style)
recipes.source_note: Greece's second most popular cheese after feta
recipes.description: Sweet, nutty Greek cheese similar to Gruyère. Often served fried as saganaki.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into small pieces.
Heat to 122°F over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Press at 30 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine 24-48 hours.
Age 3-5 months minimum.

notes: Cretan Graviera is PDO protected
Sweeter than Swiss Gruyère
Often served fried (saganaki)

recipes.title: Kefalotiri (Greek Hard Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Greek grating and frying cheese
recipes.description: Very hard, salty Greek cheese. Traditional saganaki cheese when fried.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter, ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Set 40 minutes.
Cut curd very small (rice-grain sized).
Heat to 122°F, stirring constantly.
Press firmly at 40 lbs for 24 hours.
Dry salt for several days, then brine.
Age minimum 3 months, up to 1 year.

notes: Very salty - used for grating and frying
Can substitute for Pecorino Romano
Traditional saganaki cheese

recipes.title: Bryndza (Eastern European Sheep Cheese)
recipes.description: Soft, spreadable, tangy cheese essential to Eastern European cuisine. Perfect for pierogi.

instructions.text: Start with fresh sheep's milk curd (similar to farmer's cheese).
Let curd age 5-10 days at cool room temp until slightly tangy.
Crumble aged curd and mix with salt.
Knead and press into a crock or container.
Let ferment 3-5 more days until spreadable and tangy.
Add milk if too dry. Should be spreadable consistency.

notes: Slovak Bryndza is PDO protected
Essential for pierogi and halusky
Should be creamy and tangy

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Muenster
recipes.source_note: Traditional Muenster adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Soft, smooth cheese with orange washed rind. Sheep's milk adds richness to this pungent cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Set 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Heat to 100°F over 30 minutes.
Drain and lightly press for 6-8 hours.
Brine 4 hours.
Age at 55°F, 95% humidity. Wash with brine every 2-3 days.
Ready in 3-8 weeks when orange rind develops.

notes: Washing develops the orange rind and pungent aroma
American Muenster is milder than French original
Excellent melting cheese

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Taleggio-Style
recipes.source_note: Italian Taleggio adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Soft, washed-rind cheese with meaty, tangy flavor. Sheep's milk creates even richer version.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes.
Let settle 10 minutes. Ladle into square molds.
Flip frequently for 24 hours. Do not press.
Salt all surfaces.
Age at 50°F, high humidity. Wash with brine weekly.
Ready in 6-10 weeks when soft throughout.

notes: Traditional square shape
Rind should be orange-pink and sticky
Interior should be gooey when ripe

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Reblochon-Style
recipes.source_note: French Alpine Reblochon adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Soft, nutty, washed-rind cheese from Savoie region. Traditional for tartiflette.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 30 min.
Add rennet. Set 30 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Gently stir 5 minutes. Ladle into small round molds.
Flip several times over 6 hours.
Salt and begin washing.
Age 4-6 weeks at 55°F, washing every few days.

notes: Traditional for tartiflette (potato gratin)
Should have thin peachy-pink rind
Interior should be supple, not runny

recipes.title: Sheep's Milk Limburger
recipes.source_note: Classic Limburger adapted for sheep's milk
recipes.description: Notoriously pungent washed-rind cheese. Strong aroma with surprisingly mild, creamy flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add starter and B. linens. Ripen 1 hour.
Add rennet. Set 1 hour.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Let rest 10 minutes. Gently stir, drain.
Pack into brick molds. Flip every 15 min for 2 hours.
Brine 12 hours.
Age at 55°F, high humidity. Wash with brine 2x weekly.
Ready in 2-3 months when soft and pungent.

notes: Famous for strong smell, but flavor is mild and creamy
Rind becomes very sticky and smelly
Store in sealed container

recipes.title: Classic Provoleta Argentina
recipes.source_note: Traditional Argentine grilled cheese, created by Italian immigrants in 1940s Buenos Aires
recipes.description: Grilled provolone cheese with oregano and red pepper flakes, the essential opening act of an Argentine asado.

instructions.text: Let cheese come to room temperature for 30 minutes to an hour before cooking. This helps form a better crust.
Lightly coat a cast iron skillet with olive oil and place over medium-high heat (375-400°F) on grill or stovetop.
When skillet is hot, place the cheese wheel in the pan.
Sprinkle oregano and red pepper flakes over the top of the cheese.
Cover and cook for about 5 minutes until cheese is fully melted, bubbly, and edges are golden brown and crispy.
Carefully remove from heat and serve immediately with toasted bread for dipping.

notes: Use a cast iron skillet to prevent cheese from melting through grill grates
Best enjoyed immediately while hot and gooey
For indoor cooking, finish under broiler for golden crust

recipes.title: Provoleta with Chimichurri
recipes.source_note: Provoleta served with traditional chimichurri sauce
recipes.description: Grilled provolone topped with fresh, herbaceous chimichurri sauce for a burst of Argentine flavor.

instructions.text: Make chimichurri: Combine parsley, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, and both vinegars in a mortar and pestle or food processor. Work into a thick paste.
Add salt and olive oil, mixing until you have a thick, chunky sauce. Set aside.
Set up grill for two-zone cooking with one side at high heat.
Preheat a cast iron skillet over high heat, then move to indirect heat zone.
Place cold cheese directly over high heat for 2 minutes to brown the bottom.
Transfer cheese to the hot skillet and cover until melted and bubbly, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, brush baguette slices with oil and grill until charred, about 1 minute per side.
Top hot melted cheese with a generous dollop of chimichurri and serve with grilled bread.

notes: Chimichurri can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 1 week
Hand-chopping herbs gives better texture than food processor
Chimichurri should be loose and chunky, not paste-like

recipes.title: Provoleta with Salsa Criolla
recipes.attribution: Argentine grilled cheese with fresh vegetable relish
recipes.source_note: Provoleta served with traditional salsa criolla
recipes.description: Grilled provolone served with salsa criolla, a zesty relish of fresh tomatoes, peppers, and onions.

instructions.text: Make salsa criolla: Combine olive oil, vinegar, parsley, garlic, bell pepper, onion, and tomato in a medium bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 425°F with rack in upper third.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add provolone and sprinkle half the oregano and pepper flakes on top.
Cook, flipping once, until cheese bubbles and edges brown, 4-6 minutes total.
Transfer to oven and bake until melted and golden brown, about 3 minutes.
Top with remaining oregano and pepper flakes.
Serve immediately with salsa criolla and sliced baguette.

notes: Salsa criolla can be made up to 4 hours ahead
The relish should be fresh and crunchy, not cooked
Let cheese come to room temperature before cooking for best crust

recipes.title: Ñoquis con Tuco (Argentine Gnocchi with Reggianito)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Argentine gnocchi with tomato sauce, served on the 29th of every month
recipes.description: Pillowy potato gnocchi served with rich tomato tuco sauce and grated Reggianito cheese, a beloved Argentine tradition.

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 400°F. Bake potatoes for 1-1.5 hours until very soft. Baking rather than boiling prevents excess moisture.
For tuco sauce: Heat olive oil in large saucepan over medium-high heat. Sauté onion, carrots, garlic, and red pepper until softened, 5-10 minutes.
Add tomatoes, water/stock, bay leaves, paprika, cumin, oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10-15 minutes.
Use immersion blender to blend until slightly chunky. Remove bay leaves and keep warm.
When potatoes are cool enough to handle, scoop out insides and mash until smooth.
Mix in eggs, ricotta, salt, and nutmeg. Gradually add flour, 1/4-1/2 cup at a time, until soft workable dough forms.
Divide dough into 4 sections. Roll each into 1-inch diameter ropes. Cut into 3/4-1 inch pieces.
Roll each piece over fork tines to create ridges.
Bring large pot of salted water to boil. Add gnocchi in batches and simmer 3-4 minutes until they float.
Transfer to serving bowl, top with tuco sauce and generous grated Reggianito.

notes: Día de Ñoquis: Traditionally eaten on the 29th of every month for luck
Place a coin or bill under your plate for prosperity
Reggianito is Argentina's version of Parmigiano-Reggiano

recipes.title: Milanesa Napolitana with Reggianito
recipes.source_note: Invented in 1940s Buenos Aires at restaurant Nápoli
recipes.description: Crispy breaded beef cutlet topped with tomato sauce, ham, and melted cheese. A happy accident that became an Argentine classic.

instructions.text: Season beef cutlets with salt, pepper, Reggianito, garlic, and oregano. Rub well so meat absorbs flavors.
Mix breadcrumbs in a shallow dish.
Dip each cutlet in beaten eggs, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs.
Heat oil to 340°F (170°C) in a large frying pan.
Fry cutlets until golden brown on both sides. Drain on paper towel-lined plate.
Preheat oven to 350°F (180°C).
Arrange fried cutlets on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
Spread tomato sauce over each cutlet, then top with ham slice and mozzarella.
Bake for 5 minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Serve immediately with French fries or white rice.

notes: Invented when a chef burned a milanesa and covered it with toppings to hide the mistake
The customer loved it and it became a signature dish
Can substitute chicken or pork for beef

recipes.title: Creamy Risotto with Reggianito
recipes.source_note: Classic Italian risotto using Argentine Reggianito cheese
recipes.description: Rich, creamy risotto finished with generous amounts of grated Reggianito, Argentina's beloved Parmesan-style cheese.

instructions.text: Keep stock warm in a saucepan over low heat.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pan, heat 2 tbsp butter and olive oil over medium heat.
Sauté shallot until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Add rice and stir to coat with fat. Toast for 2 minutes until edges become translucent.
Add wine and stir until absorbed.
Add warm stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly. Wait until each addition is absorbed before adding more.
Continue for 18-20 minutes until rice is al dente and mixture is creamy.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 2 tbsp butter and Reggianito. Season to taste.
Let rest 2 minutes. Serve immediately, garnished with parsley and extra Reggianito.

notes: Reggianito is Argentina's interpretation of Parmigiano-Reggiano, slightly saltier with a 5-6 month age
The key is constant stirring and adding stock gradually
Risotto should flow like lava, not be stiff

recipes.title: Pasta with Grated Sardo Cheese
recipes.source_note: Simple pasta with Argentina's sharp grating cheese
recipes.description: Simple yet flavorful pasta tossed with butter and generously topped with sharp, salty grated Sardo cheese.

instructions.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to boil. Cook pasta until al dente according to package directions. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water before draining.
In a large skillet, melt butter with olive oil over medium heat.
Add sliced garlic and cook until golden but not browned, 2-3 minutes.
Add drained pasta to the skillet and toss to coat with the garlic butter.
Remove from heat. Add half the Sardo and toss vigorously.
Add pasta water a little at a time, tossing, until creamy sauce forms.
Serve immediately with remaining Sardo, fresh cracked pepper, and parsley if desired.

notes: Sardo is Argentina's cow's milk version of Italian Pecorino, sharp and salty
The starchy pasta water helps create a creamy sauce without cream
Can add red pepper flakes for heat

recipes.title: Sardo Cheese Crostini with Sun-Dried Tomatoes
recipes.source_note: Toasted bread topped with Argentine grating cheese and sun-dried tomatoes
